info.title: Reduck REST API
info.description:
# API overview

The Reduck API is a RESTful API at `https://mcp.reduck.ai`. It allows to programmatically call browser automation scripts using an API key.

# Prerequisites

- A [Reduck account](https://reduck.ai/signin)
- An [API key](https://reduck.ai/api-keys)

post.description:
Run a saved script. `browser` chooses where: omit it (or pass `"managed"`) for a Reduck managed browser, `"extension"` / `"local"` to auto-pick your single paired device of that kind, or `{"deviceId":"…"}` to pin one exact device. Running on your own browser already has cookies for a `loggedIn` script — it is already signed in. `region`/`country` apply to the managed browser only.

What to run goes in `script` — `{host, slug, handle?, args?}` — or, to run several at once, in `scripts`: a list of those same objects. Pass exactly one of the two. **A script's `args` live inside its own entry**, never at the top level of the request — the top level configures the run (`browser`, `region`, `waitForSeconds`), not what to run.

`scripts` runs its entries **in parallel, each on its own browser**, all on the target you chose. They share nothing — separate cookie jars, separate pages, no ordering — and one entry failing does not stop the others, so the response is an array with one outcome per entry, in the order you passed them. Each is its own run and takes its own concurrency slot, so a list wider than the target's budget simply queues and drains.

Set **`sequential: true`** to run the same list as a **chain** instead: ONE browser, in the given order, so each script inherits the previous one's cookies, DOM and navigation (never its return value — outputs are not piped between scripts). A chain is fail-fast: it stops at the first script that errors, and every entry after that one reports that it never ran — you always get one outcome per script. Use it when a script depends on the browser state another one leaves behind (log in, then act); leave it off otherwise, since a chain runs one script at a time on one browser.

Synchronous by default: the response carries the outcome. A run still going after `waitForSeconds` returns `202` with a `runId` to poll via `GET /runs/{runId}` — for `scripts`, one handle per script plus a `batchId` to poll them all at once via `GET /batches/{batchId}`. A run id and a batch id are distinct: a run id always answers for that one run, even when it belongs to a batch. Both targets meter concurrent browsers and queue the rest FIFO, so a `queued` run is waiting for a slot — busy, not offline. Pass `waitForSeconds: 0` to fire and forget.

handle.description: Owner handle for a public script: "@user" for a user or "project" (without @) for a project, e.g. "reduck". Omit to run your own script.

args.description: Arguments for the script, shaped by its own input schema (see the script's contract).

files.description: File inputs, keyed by declared target filename. Either { path } — a file on the machine running the browser, so device-only: from an MCP client it is relative to the Reduck folder on your Desktop (<Desktop>/reduck/<path>, and it can't escape that folder), and it needs the extension's "Allow access to file URLs"; or the bytes themselves, which the reduck CLI uploads for you and which work on any browser, managed included.

version_id.description: Run a specific version instead of the current one. Get IDs from list_script_versions.

script.description: The script to run and its arguments: {host, slug, handle?, args?, files?}. e.g. {"host":"doctolib.fr","slug":"search_practitioners","handle":"@reduck","args":{…}}. Use `scripts` instead to run several at once.

version_id.description: Run a specific version instead of the current one. Get IDs from list_script_versions.

scripts.description: Run several scripts at once (up to 20), each on its own browser, in parallel. Each entry is its own {host, slug, handle?, args?, files?} — arguments belong to the entry that uses them, never to the run. Use this instead of `script` (exactly one of the two). They share nothing (no cookies, no DOM, no order) and one failing does not stop the others, so you always get one outcome per entry, in the order you passed them. Each is its own run and takes its own slot on the target's concurrency budget.

sequential.description: Run `scripts` as a chain instead of in parallel: one browser, in the given order, so each script sees the previous one's cookies, DOM and navigation (never its return value). Stops at the first script that errors: you still get one outcome per entry, but each one after the failure reports that it never ran. Only valid with `scripts`. Default: false.

browser.description: Where to run: "managed" (a Reduck managed browser — the only target that accepts region/country), "extension" (your paired browser extension — already logged in, so a loggedIn script needs no connector), "local" (a paired `reduck local` device), or {"deviceId":"<list_devices id>"} to pin one exact device. "extension"/"local" require exactly one paired device of that kind, else pass a deviceId.

deviceId.description: Which paired browser to run on, by its list_devices id (a per-device UUID — you may have several paired). Shorthand for browser: {deviceId}; omit to auto-pick (see `browser`).

region.description: Datacenter region (managed browser only) — pick the one nearest your target site to cut latency. One of: eu-central-1 (Europe (Frankfurt)), us-east-1 (US East), us-west-2 (US West), ap-southeast-1 (Asia Pacific (Singapore)). Defaults to the nearest.

country.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code (e.g. "FR"), managed browser only — routes the session through an in-country residential proxy so it egresses from there, not the datacenter; the lever for geo-gated sites. Nearest available is used if the exact country has none. Omit for datacenter egress.

waitForSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for the run to finish before returning a {runId, status} envelope to poll (default 60, max 110). Leave it unset: the default is right for nearly every call. 0 = return immediately (fan-out).

200.description: Run result, or a script-level error — both carry `runId`. For `scripts`, an array of these, one per script in the order you passed them (with `sequential`, the ones after a failure report that they never ran).

result.description: The script's return value (its output schema). Present on success.

error.description: Script-level error (the body threw or its output failed validation). Mutually exclusive with `result`, still returned with HTTP 200.

runId.description: Run id for tracking/replay; present on both success and a script-level error.

errorType.description: Classification of a failed run: whether the script, the caller's setup, or infrastructure caused it. Present only with `error`.

externalMessage.description: Actionable, user-facing explanation of the failure. Present only with `error`.

400.description: Invalid body, contradictory target (e.g. `region` with a device), or no device of the requested kind.

example.error: doctolib.fr/search_practitioners is loggedIn — run it on your paired browser (browser:"extension").

403.description: Out of quota for this period.

value.error: Monthly script-run quota reached: 1000 of 1000 used this period (resets 2026-08-13). Upgrade for a higher limit.
Cloud browser time quota reached: 612.4 min of 600 min used this period (resets 2026-08-13). To keep going now, run on your paired browser instead (browser:"extension"); upgrade for a higher limit.

Residential proxy bandwidth quota reached: 410.9 MB of 250 MB used this period (resets 2026-08-13). To keep going now, drop `country` to egress from the datacenter instead; upgrade for a higher limit.

404.description: Script not found or not accessible, or an unknown `deviceId`.

example.error: script doctolib.fr/search_practitioners not found or not accessible

409.description: Ambiguous target: more than one paired device of the requested kind — pass an explicit `deviceId`.

get.description:
A run's current state by id — the poll side of `POST /run`'s `202`. A finished run returns its outcome; one still in flight returns the same `{runId, status, retryAfterMs}` envelope, so you can loop on this endpoint until it settles.

Always ONE run: a run that belongs to a `scripts` batch still answers only for itself here, with its own result. Use `GET /batches/{batchId}` for the batch.

get.description:
Every script of a `scripts` request in one call, in the order you passed them — the poll side of a batch's `202`. Each entry is the same envelope `GET /runs/{runId}` returns for one run, so you can loop on this endpoint until the batch settles.

The batch stays in flight until EVERY script is terminal, then reports `failed` if any of them failed — so one script failing never cuts the poll short while its siblings are still running. The list always holds all `totalSteps` scripts, in both modes: a `sequential` batch stops at its first failure, and the scripts after it are reported as never having run rather than omitted.

get.description: List the scripts you can run: your own, those of projects you belong to, and the official catalogue. Without `handle` the list spans all three; with `handle` it scopes to one owner. One bounded page; `hasNextPage` flags more — bump `page`.

scripts.description: Search practitioners by specialty and location.

get.description: Read a script's runnable contract — name, description, visibility, loggedIn, sideEffects, and the input/output JSON Schemas (the arguments to pass to `/run`), plus the per-browser-setup success breakdown when the script has run history. Omit `handle` for your own scripts; pass a user handle ("@user") or project handle ("project", or "official" for the curated catalogue) to read that owner's public script. `includeScript=true` also returns the raw code body (not available for official scripts).
